name: Supabase
one_liner: Postgres backend platform: Management API (projects/orgs) plus per-project PostgREST data API, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions.
auth_notes: Management API: Bearer PAT (scoped or legacy) or OAuth2 authorization code (api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/authorize). Per-project data API: publishable key (RLS-limited) or secret key (bypasses RLS).
access_notes: PATs generated in account page; OAuth apps self-serve via building an integration. Free plan exists (2 active projects, paused after 1 week inactivity). Management API rate limited.

buildability.rationale: Self-serve PATs and OAuth2 for the Management API, documented rate limits, free tier, official hosted MCP. Per-project data API is PostgREST (schema-specific, key based), so scope the tool design to Management API first.

auth.quote: All API requests require an access token to be included in the Authorization header: Authorization Bearer <access_token>.
Secret key | It bypasses Row Level Security, so it must never leave your control

access.quote: Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity. Limit of 2 active projects.

api_surface.quote: Supabase provides a RESTful API using PostgREST, a thin API layer on top of Postgres.
Database Webhooks allow you to send real-time data from your database to another system whenever a table event occurs.

mcp.quote: Connecting an LLM to your Supabase projects carries security risks.

disputes.why: Free plan exists and PATs/OAuth apps are self-serve; no paid gate found for Management API.
Supabase docs publish hosted MCP at mcp.supabase.com/mcp (matches L1 removed finding).
No tier/cost gate found; only per-project design choice remains.
Ambiguity resolved: Management API (PAT/OAuth) vs per-project PostgREST (API keys) are both documented and self-serve.
Per-project data API uses publishable/secret keys.
